cases.why: LOGOS's term layer is NAMED, not de Bruijn: one `Term::Var(String)`, no `bvar`/`fvar` split. Every `Expr` in the case file is expressible — the shadowed-innermost reading directly, the shadowed-outermost reading after a freshening pass — and both kernels agree on them. The named form is what makes the second kernel worth having: `recheck.rs` converts to de Bruijn and re-derives the type independently, so a botched freshening surfaces as a DISAGREEMENT between two checkers written on two representations, a redundancy Lean has no equivalent of. The cost is real and bounded: `Context` is a name-keyed map with no stack to pop, and a binder whose name starts with `?` collides with the elaborator's metavariable convention, so an emitter owes a freshening pass and an injective sanitiser. That is an obligation on the emitter, not a term Lean can write and we cannot.

Alpha-equivalence over NAMED binders is decided by renaming rather than by index: `types_equal` compares `Var` names literally and then substitutes the first binder's name into the second's body, and `substitute_avoiding` freshens any binder that would capture a free variable of the replacement. Every shape in the case file works — five-deep shadowing, a `let` shadowing a `lambda`, alpha-variants converting — and the de Bruijn re-checker agrees on all of them. The case's second guard does not bite today: `derive_recursor` regenerates every binder it emits (`A0`, `P`, `f0`, `x`, `a0`), so a source binder spelled like a generated one is renamed away rather than merged, verified here by a constructor field literally named `A0`. What remains is a genuine obligation on an emitter — `Context::extend` is a map insert with no stack to pop, so the outer binding of a shadowed name is unreachable BY NAME — not a term Lean can express and we cannot.
